top.line: A brief for Gabriel DaCruz's Claude: his site on GitHub Pages and Google Workspace, daily interviews and a newsroom.
top.para: My brother is the family's musician and does not promote himself. His audience is on Instagram and YouTube, his album on Spotify has thousands of plays but two monthly listeners, and his site is dead. The brief gives his Claude our architecture: a repository he owns on GitHub Pages, Workspace with a mailbox for the agent, a page per work with every platform a projection, daily interviews, and a weekly brief back.

in-short.line: A brilliant musician, a dead site, the newsroom's architecture, Workspace, daily interviews, a weekly brief and a vault.
in-short.para: The web shows little of his work, and what it shows is rented. The fix: everything he owns online first, with a link; a GitHub repository he owns on GitHub Pages at his domain; Google Workspace for him and the agent; a page per work with every platform a projection; a daily interview that becomes a newsroom; and a weekly brief. The kit is in a public vault.

gabriel.line: Composer, arranger, producer, technician and conductor, with a Lisbon film concert, a school and years of gigs.
gabriel.para: He conducts orchestras, put together a Lisbon orchestra playing film music live to picture, wrote songs, set up a school and built a serious studio. We played about twelve gigs a week in the Algarve. He undersells all of it: impostor syndrome, and the trespasser's feeling of not belonging.

today.line: 10,200 Instagram followers, a YouTube channel of orchestral videos, an album on Spotify, a dead site.
today.para: His audience is on Instagram and YouTube, @gabrieldacruz_composer: more than 10,200 followers, and 145 subscribers to videos such as Live and Let Die for orchestra and the A-Team theme on bass. Spotify has an album in movements with two monthly listeners on 1 November; Apple Music and SoundCloud have pages too. His site does not load, and nothing names the concert, the school or the band.

architecture.line: A repository he owns on GitHub Pages, Claude working in it, Workspace on his domain, and platforms by embed first.
architecture.para: The site's words are markdown built to HTML, served free at his domain. Claude writes, builds and publishes on his yes. Workspace, two users (Business Standard for 2 TB of masters), connects to Claude's Gmail, Calendar and Drive connectors. Each post can go to Instagram through Meta's Graph API, linking home, and embed his Spotify tracks; Patreon has no posting API, so the agent drafts.

masters.line: Never upload straight to a platform: a master he controls, a page per work, and a copy made for each platform.
masters.para: Artists need to control their medium of distribution. Each work keeps its master in his repository, raw storage and a vault; gets a page on his site with the player, story, credits, score, sessions and related work; and every platform gets its own version, made for it and linking back. YouTube and Instagram become projections, not the place the work lives.

archive.line: First, everything he owns goes online, raw, with a link: in a month, lose every computer but one account and lose nothing.
archive.para: Every recording, session, demo, score, video and photo he owns the rights to, however old, goes to Google Drive and into an inventory, public when he is happy to publish it. Publishing raw is about solving the small problems of capture and upload, and making every piece an asset an agent can later catalogue, split and map. The weekly brief asks: is it done yet?

brief.line: A file he pastes into Claude: accounts, DNS, the repository, Google, platforms, the daily loop, reporting back.
brief.para: It walks him through a Claude plan, GitHub and Workspace; moving DNS to a host he controls with the Workspace and Pages records; creating and connecting the repository; connecting the agent's Google account. The agent's CLAUDE.md forbids unconfirmed facts, invented credits and unearned superlatives.

site.line: A first pass built only from verified facts, with nineteen items waiting for him on a public admin page.
site.para: Home, Music, Live and orchestra, Work with Gabriel, Story and News, plus an admin page on how the site is run. The concert, band, school, songs, the Spotify album's title, the award and a possible film credit wait for him; the build refuses to publish them. It is in the third person so no words are put in his mouth.

interviews.line: Interviews built around the two syndromes: ask for the specific, and who asked him to be there.
interviews.para: Ten to fifteen minutes, one topic, a voice memo counts, one artefact each time, three facts read back. First a twelve-session life story, then one question a day across his crafts, each answer a news post, the way musicians have built audiences by explaining their craft in public.

report.line: Every Sunday a public weekly brief; after the first week, a brief for me.
report.para: The agent reports what was published, which interviews happened, what waits for him and what is stuck. A brief for his brother says what was set up, what works, what it needs and three stories for the newsroom, so the work can be followed without nagging.

business.line: Setting this up for other musicians is a service he could sell, with his own site as the first case.
business.para: He is as much a technologist as a musician, and the musicians he knows share his problem: good work, a dead site, chores on every platform. A repository, a domain, an agent and a daily habit is a service he could offer them.

vault.line: A public vault with the brief, the starter kit, the interviews and prompts, screenshots and the research.
vault.para: BRIEF.md, the starter kit with CLAUDE.md, the build script, the content and the interviews, screenshots of the first pass, and the research on his public record and on what each platform allows an agent, with sources.

limits.line: His story is his brother's account; the site is a first pass, not live; prices and rules are as read on 1 November.
limits.para: The concert, school, band and award are not online and wait for his interviews. The site is not yet at his domain. The Spotify and YouTube figures come from screenshots of the apps; Instagram, Apple Music and SoundCloud from search results. Workspace prices are in US dollars and platform rules change. A film credit under a similar name is for him to confirm.

sources.line: My voice memo, the registry and DNS, his Patreon, and the platforms' own documentation, read 1 November 2026.
sources.para: The memo was recorded with Gabriel listening. Registration and name servers came from RDAP and public DNS; Patreon from its public pages; Spotify from a screenshot of the app; Instagram, Apple Music and SoundCloud from search results; the platforms and Claude's connectors from their documentation, with quotes in the vault.
